source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Predict how immunity and vaccination reduce serious infections and their spread.
node_labels: Living systems: organisms, health and ecosystems

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: A tetanus shot contains inactivated tetanus bacteria rather than inactivated tetanus toxin.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Having measles makes the immune response to a first polio infection stronger because the body remembers the earlier infection.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: The first exposure produces the stronger immune response; another exposure to the same pathogen produces a weaker response because protection was used up.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Children living on the same street have the same immunity and will fall ill equally often.

intelligence.enrichment: Immunity is the body's ability to fight disease, and vaccines help the immune system develop protection against serious infections. Vaccination builds immune protection before or around exposure, so later contact with the same pathogen is less likely to cause serious illness and can reduce spread. The learner correctly applies this rule: Immunity is the body's ability to fight disease, and vaccines help the immune system develop protection against serious infections. Vaccines are medicines taken after someone is sick, so they cure the disease rather than prepare the immune system.
